summary.text: Chrissy Houlahan is the Democratic incumbent for Pennsylvania's 6th District, which she has represented since 2019; her official biography describes her as the first woman to hold the seat. An Air Force veteran, engineer and business executive, she serves on the House Intelligence and Armed Services committees.

paragraphs.text: Houlahan was born at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, in 1967, and her official biography says she grew up in a military family.
She earned an engineering degree from Stanford University in 1989 on an ROTC scholarship and later a master's in technology and policy from MIT.
She served in the U.S. Air Force and Air Force Reserves.

In business, Houlahan helped lead AND1, a basketball apparel company based in Paoli, as chief operating officer, and served as chief operating officer of B Lab, the organization that launched the B Corporation movement.
She also taught chemistry at Simon Gratz High School in North Philadelphia through Teach for America and led a nonprofit that helps underserved students build literacy skills.
Houlahan was elected to the U.S. House in 2018.
During her first terms she served on the Foreign Affairs Committee, where, according to her official biography, she led bipartisan global malnutrition legislation signed into law in October 2022.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) she serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence (Defense Intelligence and Overhead Architecture; Open Source Intelligence subcommittees) and the Armed Services Committee (Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation; Military Personnel subcommittees).
Her official biography lists the Abraham Lincoln Leadership for America Award from the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and three Congressional Management Foundation Democracy Awards.
